info.title: Cria equipment API
info.description: Drivers → isolated compatible Cria workers → .NET API → clients. Windows rig target. Vela owns repetitions, focus decisions, solving, previews and scientific archives. Unix millisecond timestamps; RA/sidereal observations are hours; RA commands are degrees. No automatic driver restart or equipment command replay. Protocol 4 keeps the /v2 route family; protocolVersion is the compatibility signal. The service remembers only recent operations and images; a new instanceId means everything in flight before it is unknown. Images are a rolling set: the oldest are dropped when the size limit is reached, and a dropped image returns 410 image-gone.

post.description: Authenticated loopback callers only. Atomically stops new admission; rejects while operations are active. Ends state/telemetry streams and attempts driver release. Acceptance is not proof of release: the local supervisor must inspect process exit and the matching service-exit.json receipt. Never kills unresolved owners or replays operations.

post.description: The complete request identity is remembered for this service instance before anything is sent. An identical instanceId/requestId returns its existing operation; changed content returns 409 and a request whose details were dropped returns 410. No accepted request is dispatched twice within an instance; a new instanceId means earlier requests are unknown. HTTP cancellation does not cancel equipment.

get.description: Rank-2 Int32 logical pixels, first dimension outermost. No preview or processing. Served for a succeeded capture whatever the device interlock. Cria keeps only the newest images up to a size limit: an image that was dropped, or that this service instance never held, returns 410 image-gone, and the frame is lost. Never expose again to repair it. Fetch right after the capture succeeds; the file can be fetched more than once while it is held.
